notes.manual: DEFINE-UK Model Manual v1.1 (April 2026, George & Dafermos, SOAS). Contains NO policy-scenario results. Only published numeric targets are the baseline (Table 4, p.50) and scenario-design parameter values embedded in Table 5. Table 6 (pp.63-82) gives initial values for endogenous variables (2022-ish starting point) - a large replication surface for t=0 but not scenario results.
notes.paper_ssrn_6541398: Green Fiscal Policy in the UK: A Scenario Analysis (George & Dafermos, April 2026, DEFINE-UK 1.0). NOT OBTAINABLE: SSRN blocks direct fetch (403/HTML block page on abstract page and all Delivery.cfm/download.ssrn.com endpoints); no open mirror found on RePEc/SOAS/author pages. Per SSRN abstract (via search snippets) its scenarios are carbon pricing, green power sector subsidies, and green HOUSING subsidies - note: NOT 'fossil fuel ban' or 'housing regulation'. If our scenario mapping assumes a fossil-fuel ban or housing-regulation scenario, that does not match the published scenario set of this paper (regulatory/stranded-asset and public-ownership instruments were only ADDED in manual v1.1).
notes.paper_fmm2023: Earlier open version obtained: 'Green fiscal policy in an empirical UK E-SFC model' (George & Dafermos, Oct 2023, FMM conference, 'preliminary and incomplete'), https://www.imk-boeckler.de/data/downloads/IMK/FMM%20Konferenz%202023/v_2023_10_20_george.pdf (saved as fmm2023_george.pdf). Results are figure-based (Figure 3, pp.18-19); few precise numbers in text. Model version predates DEFINE-UK 1.0/1.1, so use only as qualitative/approximate sanity checks.
notes.second_paper: A second DEFINE-UK 1.1 paper exists: 'Evaluating climate policy mixes in the UK: an E-SFC approach' (2026), SSRN abstract_id=6588778 - also SSRN-gated, not obtained.

scenario_definitions.shocks: Quarterly government renewable power investment per activated unit GCF_PSGVTsce1 = 0.415 (GBP billion, 2022 prices), calibrated to generate the baseline. Government renewable investment is triggered when NFF capacity utilisation threshold sigma_NFFcap = 1.1 (ratio of NFF capacity to total electricity demand) is breached; inactive-trigger spending decays at delta_GCFPSGVT = 0.9 per quarter.

Initial ETS price multiplier phi_PETSinitsce2 = 5.5 (scaling above baseline) applied at scenario start; thereafter quarterly ETS price growth g_PETSsce2 = 0.0306 beyond the initial jump; growth formula activates T_PETSdelay = 9 quarters after simulation start; ETS coverage for production and power sectors increased by delta_COVETS2 = 0.5. Baseline ETS carbon price growth g_ETSB = 0.0001283 quarterly; baseline emission price starts ~GBP 8.01/tCO2e (2025, Table 4).

scenario_definitions.scenario: sce3 (Green Power Subsidy / government renewable power investment scale-up)
scenario_definitions.shocks: Quarterly government renewable power investment per activated unit GCF_PSGVTsce3 = 3.33 (GBP billion, 2022 prices), 'based on policy scenario design' (vs 0.415 in sce1).

scenario_definitions.scenario: v1.1 new instruments (no numeric design values published)
scenario_definitions.shocks: v1.1 adds: (i) limited forward-looking behaviour to policy announcements; (ii) regulatory policies that directly depreciate affected sectors' capital stock (stranded assets); (iii) direct government ownership of non-fossil power capital (strategic public ownership); (iv) green sovereign bond instrument financing green public investment in certain scenarios.

Implemented 2024Q1. Tax on emissions increased steadily from ~GBP 15/MtCO2e [sic, per tCO2e] to over GBP 150 by 2030. Baseline emission tax derived from OBR UK ETS revenue forecasts over all emissions.
Implemented 2024Q1. Government invests an additional 1% of GDP in green projects by 2030.
Implemented 2024Q1. Same carbon tax path as Carbon Tax Increase; all revenue recycled as green subsidies reducing the unit cost of renewable energy.
Carbon pricing, green power sector subsidies, green housing subsidies (per abstract). Numeric shock sizes unavailable.

Carbon tax alone: lower GDP growth, unemployment rises to ~4.7% by 2028-2030 (Fig 3h, approx) vs baseline ~2.7%; Green Public Investment: expansionary, unemployment falls toward ~1.5% by 2030 (Fig 3h, approx; labour supply constraint noted - larger GPI could hit 0%); CT+GS roughly neutral on GDP.
